KEY MESSAGE 1...As of 2:15 AM EDT...Sfc high pressure has 
shifted off to our south and east, with a warmer airmass aloft 
now moving overhead. Areas south and east of the Capital 
District have stayed mainly clear so far tonight, and where 
winds have been calm temps have dropped into the upper 40s. 
North and west of Albany, current radar shows a line of showers,
with overcast skies per GOES 16 nighttime microphysics RGB 
satellite product. Here, temps are mainly in the mid 50s, with 
some upper 50s to around 60 near the Capital District where S/SE
winds remain breezy at around 10 kt per latest ASOS obs. While 
this line of showers should weaken as it tracks east over the 
next few hours, we did expand footprint of slight chance PoPs 
from the NBM.

As a sfc low tracks well north of the region today, a cold front 
will track to the W/SW of the region, but washes out and becomes 
stationary there. We will see partly to mostly cloudy skies today, 
but with the warmer airmass aloft thanks to a closed 600 dam ridge 
centered over TN, temps will be above normal, with most areas in the 
upper 70s to around 80. Without any large-scale forcing, mainly dry 
conditions are expected today. The aforementioned frontal 
boundary begins to slowly lift back north tomorrow night. With 
light S/SE flow and increasing dew points, more clouds (stratus)
are expected tonight. A few light showers can't be ruled out 
either towards daybreak, especially for southwestern areas. 
Patchy fog/mist will be possible anywhere breaks in the clouds 
develop thanks to the higher dew points. Overnight lows will 
also be warmer than previous nights with most areas in the upper
50s to around 60.

On Thursday, a wave of low pressure will track along the frontal 
boundary in response to an upper shortwave. This will help lift the 
boundary back northwards as a warm front. Some uncertainty remains 
in just how far north the frontal boundary will get with a 1025 mb 
sfc high located in southeastern Canada. May need to lower temps 
from the previous forecast for the eastern ADKs/Upper Hudson 
Valley/CT River Valley with future forecasts if guidance continues 
to show the front getting hung up near the I-90 corridor. For areas 
south of the front, highs will be in the upper 70s to low 80s again 
with muggy conditions. Scattered to numerous showers are expected 
Thursday with the increasing lift and moisture. PWATs increase to 
1.75 to 2.0", and flow aloft looks fairly parallel to the warm 
frontal boundary, so some briefly heavy rain and training look 
possible, although potential for hydro issues looks fairly low with 
most areas going on a few days since the last appreciable rainfall. 
Some instability (<500 J/kg) may be present W/SW of the Capital 
District, so a few thunderstorms are possible here, but the overall 
lack of instability should also help limit the potential for hydro 
and/or severe weather concerns. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Thursday night into Friday, a fairly strong 
cold front tracks through the region as the sfc low moves off to
the east and a closed upper low drops further south into eastern
Canada. Behind the front, much cooler and less humid weather is 
expected with breezy NW winds. High pressure then builds 
overhead Friday night, leading to favorable radiational cooling 
conditions and temperatures dropping into the 30s (terrain) to 
40s (valleys). Depending on how quickly the sfc high builds in, 
temps may need to be lowered in the southern ADKs Friday night. 
Still a few days away, but will monitor for the potentially for
some patchy frost in the southern ADKs Friday night as well. 
The sfc high remains close enough to keep us mainly dry Saturday
with temps remaining below normal, mainly in the 60s.

Saturday night or Sunday, a sfc low tracking out of the Ohio 
Valley/southern Great Lakes in response to an upper shortwave looks 
to lift another warm front across the region with renewed chances 
for showers. Monday and Tuesday may remain unsettled next week, 
although confidence is low. The aforementioned boundary looks 
to linger somewhere near our region, but it is uncertain how far
north it will get with high pressure building into southern 
Canada. Near and south of the front, multiple rounds of showers 
will be possible, with drier and cooler conditions to the north
of the boundary. Will work to refine this portion of the 
forecast over the next several days.
